voiceover: You save the word café, and your friend's app shows it as caf, then two random symbols. Here's why. Computers only store numbers, so every character gets a number. In ASCII, capital A is 65 and lowercase a is 97. Unicode gives every character in every language, plus emoji, its own number: over 150,000. UTF-8 turns those numbers into bytes. English letters take one byte. The é takes two: C3 and A9. Open those two bytes with the wrong encoding, and each byte becomes its own character: an A with a tilde, and a copyright sign. The fix: save and read everything as UTF-8. Send this to whoever's app still shows weird symbols.
